euronews.description: Researchers said their findings should offer reassurance for hopeful fathers who take antidepressants.

euronews.title: Farmers demonstrate in Brussels against EU budget cuts
euronews.description: Francie Gorman, President of the Irish Farmers Association, warns that cuts to the common agricultural policy could threaten their livelihoods, food security and the future of European farming.

euronews.title: Judges in Netanyahu corruption trial urges dropping key charges
euronews.description: Israel continues to struggle to form a government after the 27 October election. Netanyahu has denied wrongdoing in all three cases since his trial began in May 2020.

euronews.title: Ashes to ashes: FC Barcelona reveals plans to let Camp Nou be fans' final resting place
euronews.description: Extra-time may soon have a different meaning for fans of FC Barcelona. Supporters are now being offered the chance to keep their ashes at the Spanish football club, under recently announced plans to build a memorial within the walls of the famous Camp Nou stadium.

euronews.title: Watch as rare cloud 'waterfall' cascades over Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro
euronews.description: The natural phenomenon went viral on social media, forcing photographers to confirm that it wasn't produced by artificial intelligence.

euronews.title: TUI boss wants EU to cut bureaucracy, attract talent and expand green energy
euronews.description: Euronews spoke with TUI's CEO Sebastian Ebel about manure-powered cruise ships, migration, dependence on the US, Artificial Intelligence, and the future of tourism.

euronews.title: Norwegian low-cost carrier Norse Atlantic suspends flights as bankruptcy looms
euronews.description: Norwegian low-cost carrier Norse Atlantic, hit by surging jet fuel prices due to the war against Iran, said on Thursday that it was teetering on the verge of bankruptcy as it cancelled all flights for the day.

euronews.title: Flames and thick smoke billow from Bangkok oil facility after massive explosion
euronews.description: A powerful explosion rocks an oil depot in Bangkok, Thailand, sending thick black smoke into the sky and prompting evacuation warnings.

euronews.title: Feminists march across Spain against violence ahead of general election
euronews.description: Demonstrations for the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women come just days before elections in which the far right could approach 20% of the vote.

euronews.title: ‘The taste layer of the internet ’: Reddit's COO on why AI needs humans
euronews.description: Euronews Next spoke to Jen Wong about the threat of AI to the open internet and the importance of human connection on the platform.

euronews.title: From Vice City to gaming suites: How Grand Theft Auto VI is changing the way people travel
euronews.description: From hotels with dedicated gaming rooms to real-life destinations featured in blockbuster titles, video games are increasingly influencing holiday plans. New data reveals a surge in searches for gaming-themed stays, with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI helping fuel the trend.

euronews.title: Images show Kim Jong Un inspecting North Korean nuclear facilities
euronews.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has called for expanding the country's nuclear arsenal after visiting nuclear material production facilities and a weapons research institute.

euronews.title: Why the Mediterranean is a hotspot for oil spills after tanker sinks near Ibiza
euronews.description: Any pollution entering the water could have a possible impact on Mediterranean seagrasses that absorb substantial quantities of climate-heating carbon dioxide.

euronews.title: Latest news bulletin | November 26th, 2026 – Midday
euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 26th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: Musk says will give two SpaceX shares to 'every child in America'
euronews.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said on Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month.

euronews.title: EU must find new revenue or scale back spending plans, MEP says
euronews.description: EU leaders are meeting in Brussels to discuss the bloc’s next seven-year budget.

euronews.title: US says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites to build data centres in space
euronews.description: The US Federal Communications Commission authorised Elon Musk's rocket company to create a data centre constellation to power AI on earth.

euronews.title: After initial reluctance, Bulgaria says it's 'ready' to join €45 billion Ukraine loan
euronews.description: Bulgaria will contribute to the new €45 billion support loan to Ukraine, Prime Minister Rumen Radev confirmed on Thursday. But the country will not help pay for weapons and ammunition.

bbc.title: German boat dealer suspected of supplying Channel smuggling gangs, BBC finds
bbc.description: Nearly a third of crossings in early 2026 allegedly involved boats or engines from the German man's firm.

bbc.title: Watch: BBC confronts German man suspected of supplying migrant gangs with small boats
bbc.description: Marvin Reuter is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

bbc.title: Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling
bbc.description: A landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) convicted Myanmar of genocide against its Rohingya minority.

bbc.title: Desperate appeals from women on death row in Iran after protests
bbc.description: Female protesters and dissidents are being sentenced to death in numbers not seen for decades, a rights group says.

bbc.title: Diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes sinks near Ibiza, killing one
bbc.description: The possible environmental damage is still being assessed by Spain's sea rescue service.

bbc.title: Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa
bbc.description: Lenacapavir, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection.

bbc.title: Tributes for Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor after his death aged 65
bbc.description: Simon Le Bon and his other bandmates say Taylor "brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music".

bbc.title: Seven injured, four critically, after Bangkok oil refinery explosion
bbc.description: Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, while officials urged residents to leave the area.

bbc.title: Hamas political official and wife among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza
bbc.description: The killings are the latest from a series of near daily attacks by Israel against what it says are Hamas targets.

bbc.title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold
bbc.description: Indonesian authorities say another 13 are missing in the illegal gold mine, which flooded on Monday.

bbc.title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats
bbc.description: Gen Kainerugaba threatened a rebel takeover of a mineral-rich area in DR Congo in controversial X posts.

bbc.title: New UK-EU treaty has 10-year termination clause
bbc.description: Text of the treaties will be published this afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.

bbc.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
bbc.description: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.

bbc.title: Guinea orders residents to clean up the capital months after deadly rubbish dump collapse
bbc.description: The capital's main rubbish dump has been closed since the disaster, leading to rubbish piling up in the streets.

bbc.title: Musk's plan to send a million SpaceX data satellites into space approved
bbc.description: The Starmind constellation aims to be the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for AI computing power.

bbc.title: Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to severe weather
bbc.description: The move represents the first postponement of the iconic event, and comes after a forecast of strong winds and heavy rain.

bbc.title: Thirty-one killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway
bbc.description: Another 21 are injured after the tanker reportedly overturns on a busy ring road in the Egyptian capital.

bbc.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
bbc.description: Officials say no lead has been detected in the surrounding area, which continues to be tested following concerns from locals.

rfi.title: French media reveal more anti-Semitic messages allegedly sent by Jordan Bardella
rfi.description: French media on Thursday revealed what was described as new evidence that the president of the far-right National Rally party, Jordan Bardella, wrote anti-Semitic messages over Facebook as a teenager. Two months after investigative site Mediapart first revealed conspiracist remarks about Jewish people allegedly sent by Bardella, the outlet and newspaper Le Monde published extracts from a 2013 conversation which they said contained further anti-Semitic comments.

rfi.title: EU leaders set for bruising battle over budget and Ukraine
rfi.description: EU leaders are set to clash Thursday over the bloc's next long-term budget and aid to Ukraine as a French ultimatum and German pressure raise the stakes before the two-day meeting in Brussels.

rfi.title: EU rejects new US tariffs targeting industrial overcapacity
rfi.description: The European Union has rejected the rationale behind new tariffs proposed by the United States on several trading partners, to fight what Washington describes as excess industrial capacity, and said it expects the US to honour its existing trade deal with the bloc.

rfi.title: Shredder-wielding Cannes mayor surges into French presidential race
rfi.description: A little-known mayor whom supporters liken to the French version of Argentina's chainsaw-wielding president Javier Milei has been catapulted into third place in France's polarised presidential race, shooting up the polls five months before the vote.

rfi.title: Romans burn PSG's perfect start to Champions League campaign
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain's flawless start to the defence of their Champions League crown ended on Wednesday night in a 2-2 draw with Roma.

rfi.title: EU plans €50bn tech fund to compete with US and China in the quantum race
rfi.description: The European Union on Wednesday announced plans for a fund of up to €50 billion to boost artificial intelligence and quantum computing, alongside new rules favouring EU companies for public contracts. The bloc aims to lead the world in quantum technology by 2030 and avoid losing further ground to the United States and China.

rfi.title: French FM defends Ukraine's attacks on Russian ships in Libya
rfi.description: France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Wednesday that Ukraine had been exercising its "absolute right to self-defence" by attacking two Russian ships in Libyan waters.

rfi.title: Moroccan football federation vows to continue legal fight over 2025 AFCON win
rfi.description: The Royal Moroccan Football Federation was on Wednesday preparing a new legal fight after the Court of Arbitration for Sport restored the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title to Senegal.

rfi.title: Israel accused of preventing births in Gaza as Amnesty seeks genocide probe
rfi.description: Israeli measures have prevented births in Gaza, Amnesty International said on Wednesday – calling for the International Criminal Court to investigate whether they amount to an act of genocide. In a report documenting the war’s devastating toll on women and girls, the rights group detailed the collapse of fertility services and deadly shortages of medicines needed during childbirth.

rfi.title: Women in France face financial hurdles to escaping domestic abuse, report finds
rfi.description: Money can be one of the biggest barriers to escaping domestic violence for women around the world. In France, leaving an abusive partner can cost a woman up to 11 months' salary in the first three months alone, a report published on Wednesday has found. Its authors are calling for greater public support, warning that the expense can prevent women from leaving or force some to return to violent partners.

rfi.title: France urged to put women's safety at heart of migration policies
rfi.description: France's High Council for Equality between Women and Men is calling for gender to be a "central aspect" of migration policies, warning that the violence migrant women suffer throughout their journeys is being ignored. The call comes as the world marks International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Police officer to stand trial for murder over shooting of French teenager Nahel
rfi.description: A French police officer who shot and killed 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk during a traffic stop in June 2023 will stand trial for murder following a ruling by an appeals court. Tuesday’s ruling is the latest in a series of competing judicial rulings over a case that has for many become a symbol of police brutality in France.

rfi.title: Gisèle Pelicot to file legal complaint against publisher over nude photo use
rfi.description: Gisèle Pelicot said on Monday she was "deeply shocked" that nude photographs of her had been used without her consent to promote a psychoanalyst's essay on the concept of coercive control.

rfi.title: France to establish 'strategic stockpiles' of critical minerals
rfi.description: France will build up "strategic stocks" of rare earths and certain priority metals, inspired by the reserves that exist for oil, the presidency announced on Monday.

rfi.title: Zambia formally indicts opposition leader on treason charges
rfi.description: Zambian prosecutors have formally indicted the country's main opposition leader and 12 others on treason charges over an alleged plot to overthrow the government. This comes three months after a contested election which saw incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema secure a second term.

rfi.title: Macron pledges €350m for aviation research in a bid for industrial acceleration
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has announced €350 million in funding for civil aviation research and plans to create new industrial zones with simplified administrative procedures, as France looks to accelerate its re-industrialisation. The announcement came during the second Choose France business summit focused on the home market.

rfi.title: Zelensky calls for EU inclusion in talks with Russia 'as soon as possible'
rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance.

rfi.title: UN condemns drone strikes in Khartoum suspected to have come from Ethiopia
rfi.description: A United Nations building was one of several structures damaged in drone attacks on Sudan’s capital, Khartoum, which are suspected to have been launched from Ethiopia.

lemonde.title: Messages antisémites de Jordan Bardella : les 19 preuves que le président du RN est bien l’auteur des propos incriminés sur Messenger
lemonde.description: « Le Monde » s’est procuré les échanges privés de Jordan Bardella sur Facebook en 2013, révélés par « Mediapart » le 28 septembre, et s’est entretenu avec son interlocuteur de l’époque. En comparaison de ses déclarations ou écrits publics, ces éléments attestent que le président du Rassemblement national a bien tenu des propos antisémites.

lemonde.title: « A l’hôpital, ils ne savaient pas si je passerais la nuit » : les grenades assourdissantes blessent toujours plus gravement les manifestants
lemonde.description: Stéphanie et Jonathan ne se connaissent pas mais, depuis le 24 octobre, ils ont un point commun : tous deux ont vu leur corps perforé par un éclat de grenade assourdissante. Des blessures qui continuent de les hanter.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Jean-Luc Mélenchon, en visite vendredi à Berlin, inquiète l’Allemagne avec sa rhétorique anti-allemande
lemonde.description: Le candidat de La France insoumise à l’élection présidentielle française de 2027, de passage à Berlin le 27 novembre, n’a à ce stade pas de rendez-vous prévu avec des élus du parti de gauche radicale Die Linke, qu’il nomme pourtant « notre partenaire allemand ».

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Edouard Philippe passe à l’offensive face à David Lisnard
lemonde.description: Sous pression de ses concurrents de droite et du centre pour une primaire, le candidat Horizons avait sous-estimé la percée du maire de Cannes. Il dénonce désormais ses ambiguïtés avec l’extrême droite et veut se démarquer de sa ligne ultralibérale.

lemonde.title: Au Royaume-Uni, le procès de Russell Brand et un autre comparable à l’affaire Pelicot ouvrent un débat national sur le consentement
lemonde.description: Dans une tribune publiée mardi dans le quotidien « The Guardian », le premier ministre travailliste, Andy Burnham, affirme vouloir réfléchir à une réforme de l’âge du consentement.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : le désarroi des partis pro-Ukraine et pro-Europe alors que ces sujets ne mobilisent pas les électeurs
lemonde.description: De Raphaël Glucksmann à Gabriel Attal, en passant par Edouard Philippe, les défenseurs d’une ligne ferme face à Moscou peinent à imposer les sujets internationaux en raison des préoccupations pour le pouvoir d’achat et la dette.

lemonde.title: Les licenciés d’Ascométal entre galère, colère et nostalgie, un an après la liquidation : « Je suis tombée très bas. C’est comme vivre un deuil »
lemonde.description: En novembre 2025, les salariés d’Ascométal apprenaient la liquidation de leur groupe, fleuron français de la sidérurgie. Un coup de massue. Un an après, sur les 481 licenciés suivis, 225 ont retrouvé du travail, mais seuls 137 sont en CDI. Tous ces anciens employés peinent à se reconstruire et attendent une réparation judiciaire.

lemonde.title: A Paris et en Île-de-France, trois adresses où les cuisines africaines brillent de toutes leurs saveurs
lemonde.description: Jusqu’ici un peu sous-représentées dans l’Hexagone, les spécialités subsahariennes ont enfin la cote et s’affichent au menu de restaurants de styles très différents

lemonde.title: Les Millionnaires patriotes, ces riches qui veulent payer des impôts, se lancent en France
lemonde.description: Espérant peser sur le débat à l’approche de la présidentielle, la branche française de l’association, créée aux Etats-Unis, ouvre jeudi 26 novembre. L’héritière Emmanuelle Oudéa et l’entrepreneur Maxime Kurkdjian sont les figures de cette campagne.

lemonde.title: Ces centaines de milliers de jeunes Indiens prêts à quitter l’Inde pour étudier : « Après l’annulation du concours de médecine, j’ai énormément pleuré. J’ai trouvé cela tellement injuste »
lemonde.description: « Inde, une jeunesse fracturée » (4/4). Après avoir quatre fois échoué au concours de médecine et subi, en 2026, l’annulation d’un examen à la suite des fuites de sujets, Prithviraj Chauhan, 21 ans, essaie désormais d’obtenir un visa pour poursuivre les études dont il rêve. Chaque année, ils sont nombreux comme lui à tenter de partir à l’étranger pour se former.

lemonde.title: Espagne : le naufrage d’un pétrolier chargé de diesel fait un mort au large d’Ibiza, sans « indice de pollution » provisoirement observé
lemonde.description: L’équipage de 17 membres a été secouru, mais l’un d’entre eux a ensuite été déclaré mort à l’hôpital, à Ibiza, selon les secours de l’archipel des Baléares. Les dommages environnementaux sont en cours d’évaluation.

lemonde.title: Transport en Ile-de-France : le point sur les grands travaux et les perturbations jusqu’à la fin de l’été 2027
lemonde.description: Environ 4 milliards d’euros seront alloués à la régénération et à la modernisation du réseau. Des perturbations sont à prévoir sur un certain de nombres de lignes de métro, tramways ainsi que sur le réseau ferré.

lemonde.title: Le Népal s’apprête à déclarer mortes les plus de 5 000 personnes disparues dans les inondations de l’Himalaya
lemonde.description: Au mois d’octobre, la législation népalaise avait été modifiée pour réduire de douze ans à environ six semaines le délai d’attente pour déclarer des disparus officiellement morts.

lemonde.title: Elections législatives en Espagne : l’Andalousie, laboratoire de l’alliance entre la droite et l’extrême droite
lemonde.description: Dans cette ancienne place forte socialiste du sud de l’Espagne et à quelques jours des élections législatives anticipées du dimanche 29 novembre, les partisans du Parti populaire et de Vox expriment leur détermination à chasser du pouvoir Pedro Sanchez.

lemonde.title: La saison de ski s’ouvre en pleine incertitude : « Avec la conjoncture économique, les Français veulent encore plus qu’avant avoir l’assurance de la neige »
lemonde.description: Les premières chutes de neige ont rassuré les professionnels, mais ces derniers doivent composer avec des Français plus attentifs à leur budget, des réservations tardives et un modèle économique fragilisé par le réchauffement climatique.

lemonde.title: Budget de la « Sécu » 2027 : les députés et sénateurs échouent à s’accorder en commission mixte paritaire
lemonde.description: Les points de vue des sept députés et sept sénateurs réunis, jeudi matin, pour discuter du texte proposé pour un budget de la Sécurité sociale se sont révélés irréconciliables, et ce premier conclave budgétaire de la saison a rapidement été déclaré « non conclusif ». Il sera renvoyé à l’Assemblée.

france24fr.title: Gaza : Israël menace de déplacer un million de Palestiniens si le Hamas ne désarme pas
france24fr.description: Jeudi, le ministre israélien de la Défense, Israël Katz, a brandi la menace d'un nouveau déplacement massif de la population dans la bande de Gaza. Un million de Palestiniens pourraient être expulsés vers le sud du territoire si le Hamas ne dépose pas les armes, précise-t-il, conformément aux exigences du plan américain.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : la côte ouest balayée par des grandes marées
france24fr.description: Une vidéo montrant un homme et son chien emportés par une vague à Cannon Beach, dans l'Oregon, a largement circulé sur les réseaux sociaux. cet épisode illustre la violence des grandes marées qui frappent actuellement la côte ouest des États-Unis. En Californie, les fortes vagues ont provoqué des inondations et endommagé des infrastructures, notamment une partie d'une jetée près de San Francisco.

france24fr.title: Ouverture du procès d'Émilie König, "l'égérie du jihad"
france24fr.description: Ce jeudi s'est ouvert le procès de celle que l'on surnomme "l'égérie du jihad". Émilie König, revenante de l'organisation État islamique, est l'une des premières françaises à avoir rejoint les rangs du groupe terroriste en Syrie dès 2012. Rapatriée en France en 2022, elle est jugée à Paris jusqu'au 30 novembre par une cour d'assises spéciale.

france24fr.title: De nouveaux éléments concernant les propos antisémites attribués à Jordan Bardella
france24fr.description: À la Une de la presse ce jeudi 26 novembre : de nouveaux éléments de Mediapart et du Monde sur les écrits antisémites attribués à Jordan Bardella, la dernière ligne droite avant les législatives anticipées en Espagne, une histoire de corsaire, et des rassemblements aux États-Unis à la frontière entre l'absurde et la poésie.

france24fr.title: Madagascar : les lois anti-avortement tuent des femmes
france24fr.description: À Madagascar, l'avortement est illégal quel que soit le motif, y compris en cas de viol, d'inceste ou de danger pour la vie de la mère. Des milliers d'avortements clandestins ont donc lieu chaque année dans des conditions souvent dangereuses, provoquant plus d'un décès sur dix selon le ministère de la Santé.

france24fr.title: Mali : les jihadistes du Jnim somment les habitants de Tonka de partir
france24fr.description: Au Mali, le Jnim, lié à al-Qaïda, laisse jusqu'à vendredi 27 novembre aux habitants de Tonka pour quitter la ville, après quoi cette localité de la région de Tombouctou sera placée sous blocus. Les jihadistes réagissent à l'installation dans la ville d'un détachement de l'armée malienne et de ses partenaires russes de l'Africa Corps. Les précisions de Serge Daniel, correspondant régional à France 24.

france24fr.title: Mali : le JNIM lance un ultimatum aux habitants de Tonka
france24fr.description: 🇲🇱 Au Mali, le JNIM donne jusqu'à vendredi aux habitants de Tonka, dans la région de Tombouctou, pour quitter la ville avant la mise en place d'un blocus. Pourquoi cet ultimatum et quelles conséquences pour la population ?

france24fr.title: RD Congo : le personnel médical contre Ebola menacé par les combats
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, les tensions sécuritaires et diplomatiques se sont accrues dans la province de l'Ituri, dans l'Est du pays. La reprise des combats entre l'armée congolaise et les hommes du CRP fait craindre une propagation de l’épidémie d’Ebola. Le dernier bilan de l'organisation mondiale de la santé fait état de 5 575 décès. Les explications d'Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula, correspondante France 24 à Kinshasa.

france24fr.title: Propos antisémites de Jordan Bardella : Le Monde et Médiapart révèlent de nouveaux éléments
france24fr.description: Deux mois après les premières accusations visant Jordan Bardella pour des écrits antisémites, Mediapart et Le Monde apportent de nouvelles preuves ce jeudi 26 novembre. Bien que le président du Rassemblement national ait une fois de plus "formellement contesté" en être l'auteur, ces éléments indiquent que les propos datant de 2013 lui sont bien attribués.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump et Mark Rutte exhortent la Russie à ne pas "étendre la guerre" avec l'Ukraine
france24fr.description: Donald Trump et le secrétaire général de l'Otan, Mark Rutte, ont appelé Moscou à éviter toute action susceptible d'"étendre la guerre" en Ukraine. Cette mise en garde figure dans une déclaration conjointe, publiée mercredi, à l'issue d'une rencontre entre les deux hommes en Floride.

france24fr.title: Israël : la Knesset adopte un projet de loi pour une comission d'enquête sur le 7 Octobre
france24fr.description: Le Parlement israélien a adopté mercredi 25 novembre en lecture préliminaire un projet de loi visant à créer une commission d'enquête sur les défaillances sécuritaires ayant précédé l'attaque du Hamas le 7 octobre 2023, à laquelle Benjamin Netanyahu s'est toujours opposé. Une annonce qui a été accueillie par les applaudissements de proches des victimes.

france24fr.title: Yémen : les Houthis "prêts à attaquer" la ville stratégique d'Aden
france24fr.description: Les forces armées yéménites ont affirmé que les Houthis s'apprêtaient à attaquer Aden, où siège le gouvernement reconnu par la communauté internationale, tout en assurant mardi 24 novembre qu'elles ne laisseraient pas tomber la ville aux mains des combattants pro-iraniens. C'est dans cette ville stratégique du sud du pays que s'est replié le gouvernement yéménite après la prise de la capitale Sanaa par les Houthis en 2014.

france24fr.title: Égypte : incendie meurtrier sur une autoroute de l’agglomération du Caire
france24fr.description: Au moins 30 personnes ont trouvé la mort mercredi dans un incendie dans un quartier populaire de Gizeh, dans l'agglomération du Caire, a indiqué le ministère égyptien de la Santé, révisant à la hausse un premier bilan de 21 morts. Au moins 30 personnes ont trouvé la mort mercredi dans un incendie dans un quartier populaire de Gizeh, dans l'agglomération du Caire, a indiqué le ministère égyptien de la Santé, révisant à la hausse un premier bilan de 21 morts.

france24fr.title: Pologne : une zone d'exclusion aérienne à la frontière ukrainienne
france24fr.description: La Pologne va instaurer prochainement une zone d'exclusion aérienne d'une largeur de quelques dizaines de kilomètres à proximité de la frontière ukrainienne, a annoncé mercredi 25 novembre un vice-ministre de la Défense. La "no fly zone" polonaise devrait permettre d'identifier rapidement les aéronefs militaires russes pénétrant dans l'espace aérien et éventuellement de les abattre.

france24fr.title: Union-Européenne : Macron refuse la baisse de budget à propos de la politique agricole commune

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2611.33304v1 Announce Type: new

undark.title: Aftershock: Untangling the Risks of Electroconvulsive Therapy
undark.description: Psychiatrists and other experts, backed by studies, maintain that ECT is safe and effective for severe psychiatric conditions including depression, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder. But some ECT patients report lasting cognitive harm and say they weren’t adequately warned of potential side effects.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

phys-org.title: Early Stone Age rock carvings in Scandinavia may have been signposts for hunting grounds
phys-org.description: Between roughly 9,000 and 4,000 B.C., artists in ancient Scandinavia painstakingly carved large, sometimes life-size images of elk, reindeer, bears and other creatures into rock faces teetering on the edge of fjords, rivers and lakes. But their meaning has long been debated.

phys-org.title: Sensory deterrents aren't a 'one-size-fits-all' solution for sharks and rays
phys-org.description: A study on how select species of rays and sharks respond to sensory deterrents has reinforced why there isn't a one-size-fits-all solution to prevent fisheries bycatch.

phys-org.title: Many buyers willing to pay more to know where their food comes from
phys-org.description: New research from Curtin University reveals many Australians are prepared to pay more for food when they know where it comes from and how animals are treated, despite ongoing cost-of-living pressures.

phys-org.title: Mathematics fact fluency interventions for students with mathematics difficulties
phys-org.description: Associate professor Jonté Myers knows that developing fluency with mathematics facts is key to mathematics proficiency. However, many students struggle to develop these foundational skills.

phys-org.title: 'King tide' waves batter California coast, soaking San Francisco
phys-org.description: Massive waves carried on king tides battered California's coast Wednesday, prompting evacuations and soaking San Francisco, but sparing feared mass disruptions to Thanksgiving holiday travel.

phys-org.title: Wildfires raze homes, displace wildlife on Australian island
phys-org.description: Wildfires have forced road closures, displaced animals and razed homes while engulfing over 10% of Australia's southeastern Flinders Island, emergency services said Thursday.

phys-org.title: Some miniature Cas12m proteins can cut DNA after all
phys-org.description: An international research group led by graduate student Hayato Morinaga, Assistant Professor Satoshi N. Omura and Professor Osamu Nureki from the University of Tokyo has demonstrated for the first time that some Cas12m proteins do have an active state capable of cutting, or "cleaving," DNA. The team also clarified the structural differences between the active and inactive variations.

phys-org.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
phys-org.description: The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-held, lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.

phys-org.title: Dragonflies feast on other insects during autumn migrations
phys-org.description: Dragonflies feast on a host of insects—and each other—during their autumn migrations, new research shows. Scientists studied dragonflies at the Pass of Bujaruelo—a 30-meter (98-foot) gap between two high peaks in the Pyrenees, through which millions of insects migrate every year.

phys-org.title: World's fastest animal could nearly double its livable territory by 2080 in the UK due to climate change
phys-org.description: Global warming and climate change could have the unexpected bounty of making Great Britain a more welcoming home for the fastest animal on Earth. The area suitable for peregrine falcons within the UK could grow by 74% by the year 2080 under a high-emissions climate scenario, a new study has shown.

phys-org.title: Sending an Australian astronaut to space is expensive. How do we work out if it's worth it?
phys-org.description: Australia is currently in talks with the European Space Agency (ESA) over potentially flying Katherine Bennell-Pegg on a future space mission. If accepted, Bennell-Pegg—who is the director of space technology at the Australian Space Agency and completed ESA training in 2024—would become the first officially funded Australian astronaut.

phys-org.title: New eyes in the sky make timber harvesting and forest conservation easier and more efficient
phys-org.description: Flying thousands of feet above northern and eastern Maine, Dave Sandilands searched for illegally dumped trash. On behalf of the New England Forestry Foundation, the University of Maine pilot was surveying both the 760,000-acre (308,000-hectare) Pingree Easement in northern Maine, home to the state's most productive peregrine falcon nesting area, and 335,000 acres (136,000 hectares) in Washington County through the Downeast Lakes Forestry Partnership.

phys-org.title: Do we really know more about space than the ocean?
phys-org.description: New discoveries are made about the world every day—a species of deep-sea fish here, a new galaxy there. There's a saying, "We know more about space than the ocean." But is this true? How do we determine knowing? Is it the number of things we have directly observed, or is it a matter of resolution?

phys-org.title: From solving to 'digesting': How mathematicians can adapt to the dramatic changes AI has brought to their field
phys-org.description: Mathematics is having an existential crisis. On Nov. 20, 2026, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic claimed that while working with the model Claude, he had solved the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the most famous problem in mathematics. This problem has stood unsolved for 167 years, and solving it could easily warrant a Fields Medal—considered equivalent to a Nobel Prize, but for mathematics.

phys-org.title: Dinosaurs likely tore meat like birds of prey
phys-org.description: Meat-eating dinosaurs probably fed by dragging their teeth backward through flesh like a saw rather than biting straight down like a dagger, new experiments suggest.

phys-org.title: Disliking AI doesn't deter its influence
phys-org.description: An aversion to artificial intelligence (AI) does not lessen the influence of the technology on people and their decision-making, according to new research from City St George's, University of London.

phys-org.title: Sweden tops global media freedom support rankings as international funding declines
phys-org.description: Sweden has been ranked the world's leading supporter of international media freedom, according to a new index. The index also highlights a decline in funding from 30 leading donor countries, despite growing threats to independent journalism worldwide.

phys-org.title: Giant deer bones may push human arrival in Ireland back by 1,000 years
phys-org.description: A team of archaeologists and scientists has uncovered tantalizing new evidence that Late Upper Paleolithic hunter-gatherers may have lived in southern Ireland around 13,500 years ago—nearly a millennium earlier than currently confirmed.

proj-syn.description: The European Union's inability to find one person to represent it in such negotiations reflects a structural failure, not a shortage of skilled personnel. That is why the EU should step aside and delegate the selection of an envoy to the United Kingdom, France, and Germany.

proj-syn.title: The Fossil-Fuel Endgame Doesn’t Require a COP Consensus
proj-syn.description: Despite the failure of this year's United Nations climate talks, there is no doubt that phasing out fossil fuels is the right goal. The only question is whether a coalition of the willing can use policy to push markets toward a faster, fairer, and smoother transition than the traditional COP process can deliver.

proj-syn.title: Who Controls America’s AI Chokepoint?
proj-syn.description: The saga of Jensen Huang's ouster and sudden return as Nvidia's chief executive has exposed a paradox at the heart of American technological hegemony. While Nvidia's AI chips give the United States leverage over China, the geopolitical power that Nvidia makes possible gives it leverage over the US.

proj-syn.title: Where Development Cooperation Still Lives
proj-syn.description: By helping developing economies build the capacity and infrastructure trade requires, the World Trade Organization's Aid for Trade initiative has contributed to a significant increase in these countries' share of global exports over the past 20 years. But the trade landscape is changing fast, and Aid for Trade must adapt.

proj-syn.title: Nvidia’s Liability Problem Isn’t Going Away
proj-syn.description: Given previous suspicions about Nvidia's engagement with China, one wonders if Jensen Huang’s admitted extramarital affairs are just a cover-up for more consequential violations and misrepresentations. Whatever the case, the problem is not limited to Huang; with his reinstatement as CEO, it involves the company's entire board.

proj-syn.title: Mapping Strategic Supply-Chain Risk
proj-syn.description: If there is a premium to be paid for resilient supply chains, who will foot the bill? The answer can be found through a three-stage approach of identifying current vulnerabilities, letting markets and public tenders price them, and then having national-security authorities intervene only where market pricing fails.

proj-syn.title: Holiday 2026 Reading List
proj-syn.description: In the bi-weekly PS Book Recommendations newsletter—available for free to all registered PS readers—we highlight insightful, informative, or otherwise compelling books, written or recommended by PS contributors. Here, we present a selection of recent works by PS contributors that are worth adding to your holiday shopping list (and your bookshelf).

proj-syn.title: The Summit of Self-Promotion
proj-syn.description: Despite claiming that world history was made in Shenzhen with the US–Russia–China Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, the trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump, and Vladimir Putin was about optics, not substance. One of the many important problems they failed to address was China’s export-led growth.

proj-syn.title: Why Nvidia Couldn’t Quit Jensen Huang
proj-syn.description: Developing AI requires tremendous coordination across firms and sectors, from the AI labs themselves to energy and computing infrastructure, as well as long-term vision and patience. Whereas much of this coordination and planning is led by the government in China, in the US, it has been driven largely by one CEO.

proj-syn.title: Chips Too Big to Fail
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration pushed for Jensen Huang to be reinstated as CEO of Nvidia to keep the stock market high, to feed a possible productivity surge, and to advance a US foreign policy built on reconciliation with China. But will Americans continue to believe in the AI miracle and this new version of Chimerica?

proj-syn.title: Amplifying the Voice of Human Limits
proj-syn.description: Tech leaders like Elon Musk have embraced Prometheus as a symbol of creation, conquest, and discovery. But the Promethean impulse must be balanced by the “Orphic” tradition’s respect for and contemplation of nature’s mystery.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of South Korea’s Semiconductor Boom
proj-syn.description: The AI boom has driven South Korea’s economic growth well above expectations, thanks to soaring demand for advanced semiconductors. But AI’s transformative potential does not guarantee that the current investment frenzy will continue, leaving the economy vulnerable to a downturn.

proj-syn.title: Is a Financial-Market Reckoning Imminent?
proj-syn.description: After a year of unprecedented AI investment, increasingly financed by debt in opaque private markets, growing unease about the industry’s future is reflected in sharp declines in the NASDAQ index and the S&P 500. But the stock market’s dependence on a handful of highly leveraged companies—and even a single CEO—is hardly the only source of global financial risk. Amid mounting fears, we asked PS contributors what to expect from financial markets in the year ahead.

proj-syn.title: The African Union’s Elusive Quest for Security
proj-syn.description: The African Union has long sought to implement Ali Mazrui’s concept of Pax Africana, but has faced persistent logistical and financial constraints. The key to making peacekeeping operations more effective is establishing a better division of labor between the AU, the United Nations, and regional African organizations.

proj-syn.title: The Achilles’ Heel of Emerging Economies’ Trade
proj-syn.description: New research shows that 23% of global goods imports in 2024 faced at least two of three vulnerabilities: product criticality, supply concentration, and geopolitical distance. Given the wide range of problems, early diagnosis and targeted action are particularly important for emerging economies with limited fiscal space.

proj-syn.title: AI Agents Could Make Big Tech Bigger
proj-syn.description: The rise of agentic AI could give a handful of Big Tech firms unprecedented power over our personal lives. Unless lawmakers and regulators act now, these digital gatekeepers could manipulate consumers, turbocharge corporate surveillance, and threaten our individual rights and civil liberties.

proj-syn.title: If the AI Bubble Is Bursting, the Fallout Will Be Severe
proj-syn.description: With the S&P 500 following the tech-heavy NASDAQ into correction territory, even as Anthropic set a record with its initial public offering, this is a good moment to compare AI stock valuations with earlier asset-price bubbles. A look back at the dot-com boom and bust of the late 1990s offers ample cause for concern.

proj-syn.title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
proj-syn.description: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.
